comparisons.peer_summary: Other consumer primarily consists of deposit overdraft balances. Net charge-offs decreased $185 million to $295 million in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by lower overdraft losses from fraud activity.
comparisons.comparison: While Citigroup provided a consolidated provision for credit losses of $276 million driven by transfer risk allowances, Bank of America provided a disaggregated view focusing on net charge-offs for the 'Other Consumer' portfolio, which were $295 million. Both disclosures relate to credit loss metrics for the year, but they focus on different components: Citigroup on the provision/allowance build macro drivers, and Bank of America on specific charge-off volumes for a consumer subset.

sentences.text: Provisions were $276 million, compared to $950 million in the prior year, primarily driven by a lower ACL build on other assets.
Net charge-offs decreased $185 million to $295 million in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by lower overdraft losses from fraud activity.

comparisons.peer_summary: Provision for credit losses rose to $1.35 billion in 2024 from $1.03 billion in 2023, primarily due to net provisions for the credit card portfolio driven by charge-offs, whereas 2023 included wholesale loan impairments and offsets from portfolio sales.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Goldman Sachs disclosed specific drivers for their 2024 credit loss provisions, though the magnitude and composition differed significantly. Citigroup reported a much lower provision ($276 million) driven by a reduced allowance build for non-U.S. transfer risk, whereas Goldman Sachs reported a higher provision ($1.35 billion) driven by net charge-offs in its credit card portfolio. Citigroup's provision decreased substantially from the prior year, while Goldman Sachs' provision increased.

sentences.text: Provisions were $276 million, compared to $950 million in the prior year, primarily driven by a lower ACL build on other assets.
The lower net ACL build was primarily due to a smaller build for transfer risk associated with exposures outside the U.S., driven by safety and soundness considerations under U.S. banking law.
Provision for credit losses was $1.35 billion for 2024, compared with $1.03 billion for 2023.
Provisions for 2024 reflected net provisions related to the credit card portfolio (primarily driven by net charge-offs).

comparisons.peer_summary: The provision for credit losses was $10 million in 2024, compared to $171 million in the prior year which included a net addition for a single name exposure that was later charged off after loan restructuring.
comparisons.comparison: Citigroup and JPMorgan both reported provision for credit losses that were significantly lower than the prior year, though the specific drivers differed. Citigroup's provision dropped to $276 million due to a lower allowance build for transfer risk, while JPMorgan's provision fell to a negligible $10 million from $171 million, with the prior year's figure including a specific single-name exposure addition. Both disclosures highlight a material year-over-year reduction in credit loss provisions compared to their respective 2023 levels.
